new_scholarship.description: The PTE x Universiti Malaya Scholarship 2026 is a one-off competition jointly conducted by Pearson Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. and Universiti Malaya that awards a single prize of GBP 3,000 towards the winner's tuition fees at Universiti Malaya. Entry is open to international students aged 18 or over, located in Malaysia or anywhere in the world, between 1 June 2026 and 31 December 2026 (MYT). Entrants must complete the Pearson entry form, write a short response about why they chose UM and their best PTE preparation tip, and apply to at least one eligible Universiti Malaya programme (Bachelor's, Master's or Doctoral) for the listed intakes. A panel of two Universiti Malaya members and two Pearson members selects the winner on published criteria and weighting, and the prize is credited to the winner's UM student account with no cash alternative.
new_scholarship.best_fit: International applicants aged 18 or over who have already decided to study at Universiti Malaya, are applying or plan to apply through apply.um.edu.my for a listed intake, and can write a clear, original statement about their motivation and PTE preparation. Because there is exactly one winner per cycle, this is a low-probability award and should be treated as a bonus on top of a self-funded or separately funded place.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to international students aged 18 years or over, located in Malaysia and outside Malaysia (the whole world). Entrants must complete the Pearson entry form with a written response, and apply to at least one Universiti Malaya programme offered through apply.um.edu.my; for competition purposes applications are available only to Bachelor's Degree, Master's Degree and Doctoral Degree programmes for Academic Session 2026/2027 Semester 1 (October 2026 intake) and Academic Session 2025/2026 Semester 2 (March 2026 intake). Shortlisted entrants must supply their PTE Score Report Code to validate that they have taken the PTE test. All communications and submissions must be in English. No minimum PTE score is published. Judging panel decisions are final and no appeal is entertained.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Judged by a panel of two Universiti Malaya members and two Organizer (Pearson) members. Published weighting: Response to Question (why the participant wants to study at Universiti Malaya) 25%; Originality of Response (originality of the top PTE preparation tip) 25%; Creativity & Originality 20%; Thoroughness and Completeness 15%; Quality of Submission (logical sequence, clarity, impact of structure) 15%. The winner is decided within two weeks of the Closing Time, announced on the @UniversitiMalaya, @studyunimalaya and @PearsonLanguages Facebook profiles within twenty working days of the Closing Time, and contacted by email at UM. The winner must respond within seven working days or the prize is forfeited and may be re-awarded, no later than ten days from forfeiture. Panel decisions are final with no appeal.
new_scholarship.notes: Awarding body is a joint competition: Pearson Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. and Universiti Malaya, not Universiti Teknologi Malaysia; this corrects the naming of the assigned slot. Confirmed from both awarding bodies' own domains on 2026-10-03: the Pearson rules page and a um.edu.my news announcement describing the PTE x UM Scholarship as entering its third year, valued at up to GBP 3,000, under a 2024 MoU. Funded at undergraduate level: Bachelor's Degree programmes are explicitly listed among the programmes available for competition purposes, alongside Master's and Doctoral. Caveat: the most recent publicly announced winner (2025 cycle, ceremony 9 April 2026) was a Master's student, but the 2026 rules admit Bachelor's entries, which is the basis for scoping this record to Bachelor's. This is a contest prize of GBP 3,000 awarded to one winner, not a fee waiver, not a bond-backed loan and not a service obligation; no bond, work requirement or repayment obligation is published. The prize is credited to the winner's UM student account rather than paid in cash, so it covers tuition only and only partially. Unresolved practical risk: the rules require an application to a listed intake (October 2026 or March 2026) while the competition window runs 1 June to 31 December 2026, so the underlying UM international application deadlines may need checking; the UM international undergraduate deadline for the October 2026 intake was not confirmed in this pass and is deliberately left out of the official block rather than guessed. UM's own undergraduate financial-aid page (aasd.um.edu.my) was unreachable this pass.

programme_detail_official.description: The PTE x Universiti Malaya Scholarship 2026 is a competition jointly conducted by Pearson Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. and Universiti Malaya, open from 1 June 2026 9:00AM MYT to 31 December 2026 11:59PM MYT to international students aged 18 or over worldwide. One winning entry receives GBP 3,000 towards tuition fees at Universiti Malaya, allocated by the University to the winner's student account. Entrants complete the Pearson entry form, answer two written prompts (why they chose UM, and their top PTE preparation tip), and apply to at least one eligible Universiti Malaya Bachelor's, Master's or Doctoral programme through apply.um.edu.my for the listed intakes. A four-person panel of two UM and two Pearson members judges the entries against published criteria and weighting, with decisions final and no appeal.
programme_detail_official.program_type: Contest prize credited to tuition fees by a university-industry partnership
programme_detail_official.coverage: GBP 3,000 one-off, applied to tuition fees at Universiti Malaya only. Does not cover living costs, travel, or non-tuition charges, and cannot cover the full tuition of a multi-year degree.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are an international student aged 18 or over and can be reached by email until the end of the judging period.
Be ready to submit one written response covering both prompts: why you want to study at Universiti Malaya, and your single best PTE preparation tip.
Have a PTE test already sat (or book it) so that you can supply your Score Report Code if shortlisted.
Submit a real Universiti Malaya programme application through apply.um.edu.my for a listed intake, and keep the confirmation reference.
Submit the competition entry form early rather than in the final days of the window.
Read the Terms and Conditions in full: they are a binding legal agreement governed by Malaysian law.
Plan on writing everything in English.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 31 December 2026 23:59 MYT closing time: entries received after the Closing Time are not eligible, and the rules place responsibility for lost or delayed entries on the entrant.
Entering without a Universiti Malaya programme application: applying to at least one eligible UM programme through apply.um.edu.my is a condition of entry.

Applying to a programme or intake that is not available for competition purposes (only Bachelor's, Master's and Doctoral for AS 2026/2027 Sem 1 October 2026 intake and AS 2025/2026 Sem 2 March 2026 intake).
Generic or non-original writing: 70% of the published weighting rewards the response itself (25% response, 25% originality of the PTE tip, 20% creativity).
Being unable to supply a valid PTE Score Report Code when shortlisted, which invalidates the entry.
Submitting content you do not own the rights to, or featuring someone without their permission, which permits disqualification.
Expecting cash: the prize is credited to a UM student account only, with no cash alternative.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The remainder of your tuition fees. GBP 3,000 is a single one-off credit and does not cover a full multi-year international degree at Universiti Malaya, which is charged in Malaysian ringgit (MYR).
All living costs for the duration of the degree: accommodation, food, local transport and utilities.
Non-tuition student charges such as the student pass, medical insurance, and any course, laboratory or field-trip fees.
The PTE test fee itself: the rules require you to have taken the test but do not reimburse it.
Air travel, visa and any pre-arrival costs.
Any tax due on the prize, which the rules place on the winner.
Currency friction: the prize is denominated in GBP but applied to a MYR-denominated student account, so the MYR credit you receive will move with the exchange rate.

submission_workflow: Sit the PTE test (or confirm you have a valid score) so you can provide a Score Report Code if shortlisted.
Choose one Universiti Malaya programme that is available for competition purposes for the listed intake, and apply through apply.um.edu.my.
Draft both written answers and score them yourself against the published weighting before submitting.
Complete the Pearson entry form at https://forms.office.com/r/DhJUnPAkSg and submit it in English before 31 December 2026 23:59 MYT.
Keep your submission confirmation and UM application reference together.
Monitor your email from October 2026 onward; shortlisted entrants are asked for their Score Report Code and the winner is contacted by UM staff.
If selected, respond within seven working days and confirm how the GBP 3,000 should be allocated to your UM account.

research_notes.logo: Used Universiti Malaya's own mark, which is the co-awarding institution that receives and applies the credit to the winner's student account, and is therefore not a different body's logo. Pearson's own mark also appears in the terms-page markup at https://www.pearsonpte.com/content/dam/ELL/pte/pearsonpte/images/logo-pearson.svg, but it was not probed within the fetch budget and is therefore not shipped.
